findings.summary: ASTM A500 is the most common US specification for cold-formed welded and seamless carbon steel hollow structural sections (HSS) in round, square, and rectangular shapes. It defines four grades based on strength requirements, with Grade C being the most widely used. The standard applies to structural tubing and is distinct from hot-formed ASTM A501. Canadian standards prefer CSA G40.21.

mechanisms.title: Grade classification system
mechanisms.explanation: ASTM A500 categorizes cold-formed carbon steel tubing into four grades (A, B, C, D) primarily based on minimum tensile and yield strength requirements. Grade C is the most commonly specified, while Grade D requires heat treatment. The grades reflect increasing minimum strength thresholds.

mechanisms.title: Material composition limits
mechanisms.explanation: The specification sets maximum percentages for carbon (up to 0.26%), manganese (up to 1.35%), phosphorus (up to 0.035%), and sulfur (up to 0.035%). Copper content is listed as optional minimum. These composition limits influence the mechanical properties and grade classification.
